summary: Mostly clear and dark until cloud moves in before dawn, with Saturn up all evening, early Draconid meteors after nightfall and a chance of valley fog at sunrise.
pick: As twilight fades, find Saturn as the steady golden point low in the east, climbing into the southeast through the evening. If you stay out, face north for an hour after dark: the Draconid radiant in the head of Draco is highest then, a night before the shower's peak.

facts.text: Three forecasts agree on a clear evening. 7Timer brings cloud to about 62% near 5 AM, while Open-Meteo shows only a brief patch of low cloud around 4 AM, so the predawn Jupiter and Moon pairing may still be visible.
A University of Connecticut study reported in May 2026 found that artificial light at night grew about 16% between 2014 and 2022, with the United States the most brightly lit country.
At opposition, as Saturn was on October 4, a planet sits opposite the Sun in our sky. It rises as the Sun sets, stays up all night and is at its brightest because it is closest to Earth for the year.

facts.text: The gap between temperature and dew point narrows from 6°F at midnight to 2°F by 7 AM, so any fog is most likely right around sunrise rather than overnight.
A July 2026 simulation study of radiation fog in Italy's Po Valley found that more aerosol particles mean more, smaller droplets that settle more slowly, keeping fog around up to 54 minutes longer.
Radiation fog forms when clear skies let the ground radiate its heat to space. The chilled air next to the ground cools to its dew point and, being dense, drains downhill to pool in valleys.

facts.text: With only scattered cloud and dry air, expect a clean orange horizon rather than lit-up clouds. The deeper blue of twilight afterwards is the time to look for Saturn rising in the east.

In July 2026, smoke from Canadian wildfires turned New England skies yellow. Smoke particles absorb blue and violet light and let yellow, orange and red through, and the thicker the smoke, the stronger the tint.
Smoke and dust particles are much larger than air molecules and scatter light by Mie scattering. The effect is strongest at sunrise and sunset, when sunlight crosses the most air.

facts.text: The shower runs October 6-10, so a few Draconids can appear tonight. Watch from nightfall to midnight, when the radiant near Eltanin and Rastaban is highest in the northern sky.
In July 2026 the Global Meteor Network found a new shower in Scorpius, M2026-P1. It identified 43 of its meteors using 114 cameras in five countries and traced them to a Jupiter-family comet orbit.
The Draconids produced storms of several thousand meteors an hour in 1933 and 1946. In 2011 watchers in Europe saw more than 600 an hour.

On October 7, 1959, Luna 3 took the first photographs of the Moon's far side. It shot 29 pictures on film, developed them on board and scanned them back to Earth, covering about 70% of the hidden hemisphere.

facts.text: NOAA's forecast issued October 7 expects quiet conditions tonight, then minor to moderate storms on October 9 when a CME launched on October 6 arrives.

The January 19, 2026 storm reached G4 after one of the fastest CMEs in decades, but its magnetic field (Bz) turned strongly northward. That limited the energy reaching Earth, and auroras stayed mostly at high latitudes.

Even on the October 9 storm night, NOAA's top forecast of Kp 5.67 is below the level usually needed here. A camera on a long exposure, aimed north from a dark spot, will pick up faint red glow that the eye misses.
